title: G-SpNN: GPU-Accelerated Passivity Enforcement for S-Parameter Modeling with Neural Networks
problem: Passivity enforcement in high-frequency circuit macromodeling encounters convergence issues and accuracy compromises; the Domain-Alternated Optimization (DAO) framework requires additional optimization but suffers from high memory consumption and slow convergence for large-scale problems.
motivation: High-frequency circuits require efficient and accurate passive macromodeling, but existing passivity enforcement methods create computational bottlenecks that limit scalability to complex circuits.
method: G-SpNN recasts passivity-enforced macromodeling as a neural network training problem, leveraging GPU acceleration to significantly enhance convergence speed and memory efficiency. The approach translates domain constraints into neural network regularization objectives.
key_novelty: Reformulating passivity enforcement as neural network training enables GPU acceleration and overcomes memory/convergence bottlenecks of traditional optimization-based methods.
contributions: GPU-accelerated framework for passivity-enforced S-parameter macromodeling
Reformulation of domain constraints as neural network training objectives
7.63x average convergence speedup compared to DAO
Two orders of magnitude memory usage reduction, enabling handling of high-port-count circuits
limitations: Abstract does not discuss passivity guarantees in the final neural network model, generalization to different frequency ranges, or comparison with recent machine learning macromodeling approaches.
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated neural network approach to passivity-enforced circuit modeling
